introduction: ERC-6617 defines a bit-based permission and role system in which each permission is a single bit of a uint256, encoding up to 256 permissions that combine into roles. It was proposed by Chiro and Victor Dusart in February 2023. Each permission must be a power of two so it occupies one bit, and the interface exposes functions to grant, revoke, and check permissions with bitwise operations, emitting an event on each change. Note: ERC-6617 is in Review status; the interface may still change before it is finalized.
designPurpose: ERC-6617 was designed to make on-chain access control more granular and gas-efficient than single-owner or string-based role schemes. Under ERC-173 a contract has one owner, and role systems keyed on bytes32 identifiers need a storage read per check. By packing every permission into one bit of a uint256, ERC-6617 tests access with a single bitwise AND and merges permissions into roles with bitwise OR, avoiding extra storage loads. Ordering bits by significance also lets permissions be ranked as integers.
commonUsage: Bit-based permissions suit contracts that need distinct access levels, such as multi-role protocol administration, minting and pausing rights on a token, or module permissions in a smart-contract account. Because roles are plain uint256 values, they can be passed between contracts and compared without storage lookups. ERC-6617 also defines an optional IEIP6617Meta extension that attaches a name and description to each permission for explorers and dashboards to display.
fn.hasPermission.desc: Returns true when the user's stored permission bitmask is a superset of the required permission, meaning every bit set in _requiredPermission is also set for the user. The check is a view operation using a bitwise AND.
fn.hasPermission.params._user: Address of the user whose permission is checked.
fn.hasPermission.params._requiredPermiss: The permission, or combination of permission bits, that the user must hold.
fn.hasPermission.returns.result: True if the user's permission is a superset of the required permission, otherwise false.
fn.grantPermission.desc: Adds the given permission bit to the user's bitmask with a bitwise OR and emits a PermissionGranted event. The permission to add must be a power of two so it sets exactly one bit.
fn.grantPermission.params._user: Address of the user to whom the permission is added.
fn.grantPermission.params._permissionToA: The permission bit to add; it must be a power of two.
fn.grantPermission.returns.success: True when the permission has been granted.
fn.revokePermission.desc: Removes the given permission bit from the user's bitmask and emits a PermissionRevoked event, leaving the user's other permissions intact.
fn.revokePermission.params._user: Address of the user from whom the permission is revoked.
fn.revokePermission.returns.success: True when the permission has been revoked.
fn.PermissionGranted.desc: Emitted when a permission is granted to a user, recording the grantor, the permission, and the receiving user.
fn.PermissionGranted.params._user: Address of the user who received the permission.
fn.PermissionRevoked.desc: Emitted when a permission is revoked from a user, recording the revoker, the permission, and the affected user.
fn.PermissionRevoked.params._user: Address of the user who lost the permission.
sim.grantPermissionWalkthrough.name: Grant Permission Walkthrough
sim.grantPermissionWalkthrough.desc: Follow a grantPermission call from the grantor through the permission bitmask to the PermissionGranted event.
sim.grantPermissionWalkthrough.step.call: The grantor calls grantPermission(_user, _permissionToAdd) with a permission that is a power of two, targeting the user who should receive the access bit.
sim.grantPermissionWalkthrough.step.exec: The contract ORs the new permission bit into the user's stored uint256 bitmask, so any bits already granted are preserved.
sim.grantPermissionWalkthrough.step.even: The contract emits PermissionGranted with the grantor, permission, and user, and the target user now holds the added permission.
